sections.overview: It is a Mexican tarantula. Its natural range is a small coastal strip of western Guerrero east of the Balsas River.
sections.identification: Adult body length is about 70 mm in females and 60 mm in males, on average. The CITES guide contrasts it with B. auratum: boehmei has orange-red patellae, tibiae and metatarsi, whereas auratum has dark legs with a flame-shaped mark on the patella.
sections.habitat: It lives in dry forest and thorn scrub, sheltering in shallow burrows under rocks and roots.
sections.diet: At night it hunts ground arthropods and occasionally small vertebrates around the entrance to its shallow burrow.
sections.behavior: It hides by day, then waits at the burrow entrance after dusk to catch passing prey.
sections.reproduction: Males search for females from late rains into the dry season, roughly August through January.
sections.ecology: It is closely related to other Mexican red-legged Brachypelma, including B. baumgarteni and the nearby B. smithi; compared with those relatives, its narrow coastal or inland range makes the local forest belt especially important.
sections.conservation: It is listed in CITES Appendix II, which regulates international trade in the genus; the listing is a trade control rather than a ban on all keeping.
